evidence: server.mjs:88-93 — abilities route isolated in a 5-line handler
views.mjs:250-276 — renderAbilityPage a single function, but lives in a 620-line monolith
views.mjs:563 — abilities links from the Pokémon page require editing an unrelated renderer
views.mjs:602-606 — dead renderAbilityPageByName survives a route-only deletion
render.mjs:74 — ability-specific 'hidden' flag on the generic pokemonCard; styles.css:257 its orphaned CSS class
removability.rationale: The route is a clean delete, but the feature leaks into the Pokémon page renderer, the shared card component, the API layer and CSS, and pre-existing dead exports mean a lazy removal leaves code behind. Textbook 'handful of scattered edits'.

evidence: render.mjs:65-74 — pokemonCard is the single card implementation; every list goes through it
api.mjs:46 — spriteUrl is the one sprite-URL seam (used at render.mjs:69 and views.mjs:557)
render.mjs:100-115 — homeUrl canonicalizes query params once, shared by pagination links (render.mjs:108-110) and HX-Push-Url (server.mjs:61)
views.mjs:153-158, 223-237, 254-265 — the pokemon-references→species-cards pipeline is triplicated with variations, so a change to it needs three edits
changeability.rationale: The highest-traffic bug surface (cards, sprites, filter URLs) lands in one obvious place thanks to pokemonCard/spriteUrl/homeUrl. Below a 5 because the card-list construction and the type/move/ability 'resolve species, build cards' logic is duplicated rather than shared.

evidence: server.mjs:37-113 — routes contain no rendering logic; htmx partial negotiation is explicit header checks
views.mjs:1-33 — imports 18 symbols from api.mjs; views both fetch (getHomeData views.mjs:37, getPokemonPageData views.mjs:534) and render
server.mjs:57-64 — server also fetches for other routes, so fetch responsibility is split inconsistently with views.mjs:596-612 which duplicates it (dead)
api.mjs:15-33,175-189 — data layer also owns humanize/formatDex/statLabel; render.mjs:1 imports display helpers from it
views.mjs:596-612, api.mjs:42, api.mjs:192 — five exported symbols are never used anywhere
coupling.rationale: Module roles are real and interfaces are mostly narrow (views take plain data objects; renderers return strings), and server/client boundaries are clean. But api.mjs is a grab-bag, views.mjs mixes data prep with rendering for every page, and dead duplicates of server logic erode the seam between them.

evidence: render.mjs:86-91, 95-98, 77-90 — cardGrid, section and typeBadges stretch across every page without flag creep
api.mjs:96-107 — memoize is a genuine small abstraction, but versionGroupCache (api.mjs:135-142) reimplements the same idea separately
views.mjs:196-211, 234-247, 269-275 — the three card-page bodies (h1 + count + section + cardGrid) are copy-paste variations, not a shared shape
views.mjs:254-263 — ability page reimplements id extraction/hidden-map instead of reusing dedupeSortedPokemonEntries (views.mjs:139)
views.mjs:214 — moveFact dl pattern is a local const; an Items page would have to copy it
abstraction_design.rationale: The low-level primitives are well-chosen and cover real variation, but the mid-level abstractions stop short: no shared 'list of Pokémon cards' or 'facts dl' composition, so similar-but-different pages are assembled by copy-paste. Some flag creep (partial at views.mjs:87, hidden at render.mjs:65) but nothing egregious.

findings.issue: renderMovePageByName / renderAbilityPageByName / renderTypePageByName are exported but never called; server.mjs:57-98 re-implements the same fetch-and-render inline. Anyone editing one path won't find the other.
findings.suggestion: Delete the dead wrappers (or route through them in server.mjs so the logic lives in one place).

findings.issue: The pokemon-references→species-cards pipeline is written three times with variations (type page views.mjs:153-158, move page views.mjs:223-237, ability page views.mjs:254-265 including its own id extraction).
findings.suggestion: Extract one helper (on top of dedupeSortedPokemonEntries) that takes pokemon entries plus the species catalog and returns sorted card objects, with an optional hidden-ability map.

findings.issue: The 'data layer' is a grab-bag: base URL, caching, resource getters, humanize/formatDex/statLabel display helpers and English-text extraction all live together, and render.mjs:1 imports display helpers from it.
findings.suggestion: Split display formatting (humanize, formatDex, formatValue, statLabel, spriteUrl) into its own module so the fetching layer has one reason to change.

findings.issue: Three separate caching mechanisms exist in one file: fetchJson's cache/pending maps (api.mjs:30-60), versionGroupCache (api.mjs:135-142), and memoize (api.mjs:96-107). A caching-rule change (TTL, invalidation) touches all three.
findings.suggestion: Route versionGroupCache through apiGet's cache or memoize so cache policy is defined once.

findings.issue: views.mjs is a 620-line monolith mixing data preparation (getHomeData, getPokemonPageData, getMovesData) with rendering for all six pages, which is where most edit scenarios pay their tax.
findings.suggestion: Split per page (or at least data prep from renderers); page-level files make removal and addition one-file operations.

findings.issue: The generic pokemonCard carries an ability-specific 'hidden' flag whose only consumer is the ability page (views.mjs:263), so removing Abilities means editing the shared component and orphaning styles.css:257.
findings.suggestion: Accept optional trailing content/children, or let the ability page pass pre-rendered extras, so the component stays feature-agnostic.

findings.issue: Static assets are hand-served via boot-time file reads and three explicit routes; each new asset needs another route plus a readPublicFile entry.
findings.suggestion: Use @hono/node-server's serveStatic for /styles.css, /tokens.css and /htmx.min.js (it is already a dependency), keeping one place that serves /public.

findings.issue: Dead exports: englishEffect (api.mjs:42) and typeDisplayName (api.mjs:192) are exported but unused, adding noise to the module's real surface.
findings.suggestion: Delete them, or inline where the intent actually applies.

summary: A clean three-layer shape (routes / data / render) with genuinely good low-level primitives — pokemonCard, cardGrid, section, homeUrl and the memoized catalogs — that make the most common edits one-file changes. The mid-level is the weak spot: views.mjs is a 620-line data-plus-render monolith with triplicated card-list construction, the API module doubles as a formatting library, and dead by-name wrappers duplicate the server's route logic. Everyday fixes land easily; adding, removing or reshaping a page means scattered edits and copy-paste.
